newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul Exchange to list paint maker Bayrakli.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul Exchange to list paint maker Bayrakli.

text.p: The Istanbul Stock Exchange said it would list publicly owned shares of paint and varnish producer Bayrakli Boya ve Vernik Sanayii A.S. on the national market at an opening price of 7,500 lira per 1,000 lira nominal value on Friday.
The company had last week floated 160 billion lira of new shares, or 34.78 percent of its capital in a two-day public offer when raising its capital to 460 billion lira from previous 300 billion.

Turkish Global Securities, leader of the consortium which managed the public offer, said 128 billion lira, or 80 percent of the offer was sold to 27 foreign financial institutions and 32 billion lira to 28,584 domestic investors.
It added that U.S. Bank Santander and U.K.'s Genesis Investment Management each bought 18.5 billion lira worth of shares while Moore Capital of the U.K. bought 15.75 billion.
All of the offering was underwritten by Global.
Bayrakli Boya, which specialises in furniture painting and is owned by one of Turkey's leading paint and food groups Yasar Holding, holds a 21 percent share in the domestic market.
The company announced that 1.2 billion lira of the income from the public offer would be used to finance short-term debts while the rest would be spent on ongoing investments.
Bayrakli Boya raised its 1996 net profits to 148 billion lira and net sales to 3.38 trillion lira, up from 60.6 billion and 2.03 trillion lira in 1995.
